properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js (used by elliptic) provides SHA-1/SHA-2 family hashes to the shipped JS build; no direct application call site read here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: md-5 is a dependency of hash.js (elliptic's hashing layer); collision-broken MD5 ships in the build. No direct application call site read here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1@0.6.0 is a dependency of hash.js (elliptic's hashing layer); collision-broken SHA-1 ships in the build. No direct application call site read here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey is a transitive npm dependency (lockfile only) — the OpenSSL single-round MD5 EVP_BytesToKey KDF shipped in the build via browser crypto shims; no direct application call site in this repo's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: create-ecdh (npm, via crypto-browserify) declared in package-lock.json; elliptic-based ECDH also present in the exit-tool's yarn.lock. Classical ECDH — harvest-now-decrypt-later. Dependency inventory; no direct application call site read here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.16.20 (Cargo.lock) exposes X25519 for rustls TLS key exchange; an npm X25519 implementation is also declared in package-lock.json. Classical key agreement — harvest-now-decrypt-later. Dependency inventory; no direct application call site read here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 is zkSync's pervasive hashing primitive: ethers keccak256/solidityKeccak256 for storage slots and Merkle roots in contracts scripts/tests, EMPTY_STRING_KECCAK constants and KECCAK256 opcodes in compiled contract artifacts (old_contracts/ZkSync.json), Rust tiny-keccak in core. All sampled sites genuine; quantum impact limited to Grover's square-root speedup.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js 3.0.1 declared in root package-lock.json, sdk/zksync.js/package-lock.json and exit-tool yarn.lock (ethers' KDF for encrypted JSON keystore wallets), plus the Rust scrypt crate in Cargo.lock. Dependency inventory: what the build ships; no direct application call site read here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl 1.0.3 dependency (package-lock.json) — its secretbox provides XSalsa20-Poly1305. Dependency inventory: presence in the shipped build; no direct application call site read here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real call site: contracts/scripts/server-add-erc20.ts:16 does jwt.sign({sub:'Authorization'}, process.env.ADMIN_SERVER_SECRET_AUTH, {expiresIn:'1m'}) — with a string secret jsonwebtoken defaults to HS256 (HMAC-SHA256, Grover-affected, quantum-vulnerable MAC). Also the Rust jsonwebtoken crate in Cargo.lock for the API server's auth middleware. Secret comes from env (ADMIN_SERVER_SECRET_AUTH), not hardcoded.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 declared both as the Rust crate (Cargo.lock, RustCrypto PBKDF2) and the npm pbkdf2 package (package-lock.json, used by crypto-browserify). Password KDF present in both halves of the shipped build; iteration parameters live inside the libraries, not pinned in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The `openssl` crate in Cargo.lock (line 5306), reached via native-tls/reqwest: OpenSSL primitives (RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, AES, SHA) ship in the Rust build. Dependency inventory; no direct application call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jws (JSON Web Signature) npm package in package-lock.json — the JWS produce/consume layer under jsonwebtoken, which signs the admin auth token in contracts/scripts/server-add-erc20.ts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jwa (JSON Web Algorithms) npm package in package-lock.json — implements the JWS algorithms (HS256 HMAC-SHA256 default, RS256, ES256) under jsonwebtoken/jws.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls in Cargo.lock provides TLS 1.3 (and 1.2) with classical key exchange only (X25519/P-256/secp384r1) in the pinned versions — no hybrid/PQ group offered; harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to any TLS 1.3 traffic. tls_sessions found no explicit session configuration in this tree, so library defaults govern.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto k256 crate (secp256k1) in Cargo.lock — a second, distinct secp256k1 implementation in the shipped Rust build, separate from the `secp256k1` crate that eth_signer uses. Shor-vulnerable ECDSA/keys available wherever this crate is reachable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The jwa npm package is the JWA implementation — the same logical asset as the JWA object; keeping one reference avoids double-counting the package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The openssl crate in Cargo.lock:5306 — the same entry ALG-09fdf35b records; the shipped Rust build links OpenSSL via native-tls (reqwest default) for outbound HTTPS.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto sha1 crate, two version entries in Cargo.lock (7318, 7324) — collision-broken SHA-1 ships in the Rust build as a transitive dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The jws npm package is the JWS layer in package-lock.json, used by jsonwebtoken — the same logical asset as the JWS object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto hmac crate, three entries in Cargo.lock — HMAC (Grover-affected MAC) ships in the Rust build; feeds jsonwebtoken's HS256 and PBKDF2 paths.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls in Cargo.lock — the Rust TLS stack (TLS 1.3/1.2, classical X25519/P-256 key exchange, no PQ groups in the pinned versions); no explicit TLS session configuration exists in this tree, so defaults govern any rustls-backed client.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: native-tls in Cargo.lock — the default TLS backend for the reqwest 0.11 clients used by api_client, notifier, prover_utils, eth_signer and the witness generator; on Linux it terminates at OpenSSL with classical key exchange. tls_sessions found no explicit session setup, so these are library defaults.
